claims.claim: Spells, magic items, and artifacts are italicized and treated as titles, and the effect a spell creates is not italicized.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: A stat block name is bolded in running text only at its first appearance in an encounter area, and nothing may sit between the number and the name.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: Rules prose uses numerals for points, damage, durations of game effects, and tactical distances, but spells out narrative quantities (six hours, fifty miles).
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: The two cities are fifty miles apart.

claims.claim: The guide fixes verb-noun pairings: you cast a spell, take damage, make a saving throw, finish a rest, score a critical hit.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: Rules must say 'succeed on a DC 15 check', not 'make a DC 15 check', unless the outcomes follow immediately.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: “You must succeed on a DC 15 Strength check

claims.claim: 'Save' for 'saving throw' is used sparingly, mainly in stat blocks; the 4E sense of 'save' as a successful saving throw is abandoned.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: use it sparingly, preferably only in a stat block

claims.claim: 'Result' no longer means the number on the die; it means the die roll plus modifiers, and 'total' is often preferred.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: 'Magic' is the adjective for objects (magic item, magic sword); 'magical' for other things; 'magical item' is forbidden.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: “magic item” and its variants should never be “magical item.”

claims.claim: Damage is written as '10 fire damage', never '10 points of fire damage'.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: Avoid referring to points of damage

claims.claim: The die expression stays with the damage type: 'an extra 1d4 fire damage'.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: One is proficient 'in' a skill, language, or activity but 'with' a tool, weapon, or armor.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: 'Dungeon Master' is never a verb except in conversational web writing.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: This term is a noun, not a verb

claims.feature: weeks and months banned in rules
claims.claim: Because week and month lengths vary by world (a Realms week is a tenday), rules durations are given in days or years, never weeks or months.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: say a game effect lasts for 7 days, not 1 week

claims.claim: 'Human' is not a synonym for 'mortal', and 'humanoid' is used cautiously because it names a creature type.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: Beware of using “human” as a synonym for “mortal.”

claims.claim: A word list fixes spellings and plurals: dwarves not dwarfs, mithral not mithril, staffs, war band, drow/kenku/yuan-ti unchanged in plural.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
